post.title: You are 13.8 billion years old 🌌
post.description:
Send this to someone who feels small today 💫

The hydrogen in your body formed in the early universe. Your carbon, oxygen, iron and calcium were made inside stars.
post.pinned_comment: Does this make you feel small… or huge? 🌌👇

scenes.narration: You are not twenty, or thirty, or fifty years old. You are 13.8 billion years old.
Look closer. Your body is made of about seven octillion atoms.
Most of them are hydrogen. And every hydrogen atom inside you was born in the first moments of the universe.
The rest came later. Giant stars crushed hydrogen together in their burning hearts, and forged carbon, oxygen and nitrogen.
When those stars died, they exploded, and scattered those atoms across the galaxy.
Billions of years later, that dust gathered around a young sun, and became a planet.
The planet made oceans. The oceans made life.
And life, after four billion years of trying, made you.
The iron in your blood was once inside a dying star.
The calcium in your bones was cooked in stars long before the Sun was even born.
So the next time you feel small, remember. You are not just living in the universe. You are a tiny piece of it, that woke up, and looked around.
